page: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v7 is a general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, backed by 384 GB of memory (4 GB per vCPU). The instance incorporates 5,669 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Advanced instruction set support includes AVX-512 extensions (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16), AES, and SHA_NI for hardware-accelerated vector computation and cryptography.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong processing capacity. In stress-ng tests, multi-core CPU performance reaches top-tier classification with 176,145.96 operations, complemented by a single-core score of 3,792.98. Cached memory read throughput measures 9,486.57 GB/sec, while uncached large-block write operations reach 174.65 GB/sec. High-concurrency data operations achieve notable throughput, evidenced by 140.26 million Redis SET operations per second and 39,508.94 in PassMark database operations. CPU-based small LLM prompt processing reaches 5,540.41 tokens per second.

Featuring a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio combined with high-capacity local NVMe storage, the D96ads_v7 provides high resource density without requiring supplementary storage attachments. Hardware tradeoffs include the absence of dedicated GPUs for matrix-heavy acceleration and lower relative throughput on 70B parameter LLM inference compared to dedicated hardware accelerators. Suitable workloads include high-concurrency web applications, relational and key-value database engines, microservices clusters, and CPU-bound ETL pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v7 is a general-purpose instance driven by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It provides 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores, 384 GB of RAM, and 5,669 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage. Featuring hardware vector support such as AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, it performs efficiently across compute and data tasks. In benchmarks, the server achieves top-tier results in multi-core compute (176,145.96 stress-ng ops) and executes 140.26 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance offers resource efficiency by combining balanced compute and memory density with local storage capabilities. Although lacking GPU hardware, its core capacity and local NVMe storage suit enterprise database workloads, containerized application clusters, real-time analytics, and CPU-based AI inference.
